words_to_read_new.meaning: ac- means towards + cur means care + -ACY means quality: the quality of working with care towards the exact answer
liter means letters + -ACY means quality: the quality of knowing letters well enough to read and write
numer means number + -ACY means quality: the quality of working confidently with numbers
priv means one's own + -ACY means state: the state of keeping something as your own, away from others
ad- means to + equ means equal + -ACY means state: the state of being equal to what is needed
delic means fine or dainty + -ACY means quality: the quality of being fine and easily damaged
candid means white or shining + -ACY means state: the state of standing openly for a position
im- means not + medi means middle + -ACY means state: nothing in the middle, so it happens right now
suprem means highest + -ACY means state: the state of being the highest of all
con- means together + spir means breathe + -ACY means act: the act of breathing together in secret
ad- means to + voc means voice + -ACY means act: the act of giving your voice to support a cause
diploma means a folded official paper + -ACY means skill: the skill of handling talks between countries carefully

sessions.wtr_new_notes:
READ each word as it appears. -ACY names a QUALITY or a STATE.
accuracy - ac- means towards + cur means care + -ACY means quality: the quality of working with care towards the exact answer.
literacy - liter means letters + -ACY means quality: the quality of knowing letters well enough to read and write.
numeracy - numer means number + -ACY means quality: the quality of working confidently with numbers.
privacy - priv means one's own + -ACY means state: the state of keeping something as your own, away from others.
adequacy - ad- means to + equ means equal + -ACY means state: the state of being equal to what is needed. Just enough.
delicacy - delic means fine or dainty + -ACY means quality: the quality of being fine and easily damaged.
candidacy - candid means white or shining + -ACY means state: the state of standing openly for a position.
immediacy - im- means not + medi means middle + -ACY means state: nothing in the middle, so it happens right now.
supremacy - suprem means highest + -ACY means state: the state of being the highest of all.
conspiracy - con- means together + spir means breathe + -ACY means act: the act of breathing together in secret. A secret plan.
advocacy - ad- means to + voc means voice + -ACY means act: the act of giving your voice to support a person or a cause.
diplomacy - diploma means a folded official paper + -ACY means skill: the skill of handling talks between countries carefully.
Memory hook: three jobs this week - -ACY names a state, -ULE makes it small, MEGA- makes it a million. Today, hear -ACY and ask what state it is in.
SOURCES: -acy card meaning teacher-confirmed 20 Jul 2026; word meanings checked against the Macquarie Dictionary.

new_morph_activity.title: Build the -acy word
new_morph_activity.rule: Change each -ate word into its -acy word, then finish the meaning.
new_morph_activity.example: One done for you: accurate + -acy = accuracy, meaning the quality of being exact
items: 1. private + -acy = ______ , meaning ______
2. literate + -acy = ______ , meaning ______
new_morph_activity.notes:
ANSWER: 1. privacy - the state of keeping it to yourself. 2. literacy - the quality of being able to read and write.
1. SAY: "Write the new word, then finish the meaning after the comma."
2. TIME: 3 minutes. Work on your own whiteboard.
3. CIRCULATE: if a student is stuck, SAY: "Point to the example. Accurate dropped its -ate and took -acy." Then build number 1 together.
4. SCAN four boards. 80%+ -> reveal the check slide. Less -> build number 2 together, then re-check.
TRAP: writing privateacy. Fix: cover the -ate ending, then join -acy to what is left.
STRETCH: Build the -acy word from delicate and say what quality it names.
HELP: Give privacy and literacy as a word bank; students match each one to its base.

Purpose: build the -ate to -acy pattern before students use it in writing. [You Do | Word building | Morphology]

grammar.header_notes:
PURPOSE: Move from last week's identifying to adding an adverbial that tells when.
PREP: Whiteboards out before the I do.

i_do.title: Add a when detail
i_do.rule: An adverbial tells when, where, how or why. A fronted adverbial takes a comma.
i_do.example: The circuit worked. + during the test -> During the test, the circuit worked.
items: During the test tells WHEN.
It sits at the front, so it takes a comma.
i_do.routine: Eyes on me - watch where the detail lands
i_do.footer: Add the detail, then check the comma
i_do.notes:
ANSWER: During the test, the circuit worked.
1. SAY: "An adverbial tells when, where, how or why. Today we add one to a plain sentence to make it more exact."
2. MODEL: Point to during the test. SAY: "It tells when, and I have put it at the front, so I hear a small pause and write a comma."
3. ASK: "What does during the test tell us?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: when.
4. ASK: "Why is there a comma after it?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: the adverbial is at the front.
TRAP: adding the detail but leaving out the comma. Fix: reread the opening, hear the pause, then write the comma.
---
Purpose: restate last week's rule, then model adding a when detail. [I Do | Explicit modelling | Grammar | HITS 3]

we_do.title: Add it at the end
we_do.rule: Add the given adverbial. At the end it usually needs no comma.
we_do.example: The class listened. + in complete silence
items: Write the whole new sentence.
Decide whether a comma is needed.
we_do.routine: Whiteboards - Write it... Chin it... Show me.
we_do.footer: Stem: In complete silence tells us how
we_do.notes:
ANSWER: The class listened in complete silence. No comma is needed.
1. SAY: "Add in complete silence to the sentence, then decide about the comma. Write it... chin it... show me."
2. TIME: 20 seconds, then every board up together.
3. SCAN the back row first. 80%+ -> take the reason. Less -> say the sentence aloud together, then re-collect all boards.
4. ASK: "How do you know in complete silence is the adverbial?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: it tells how the class listened.
TRAP: putting a comma in front of an end adverbial. Fix: read it smoothly, delete the comma, then show the board again.
---
Purpose: guided addition at the end with a complete board response. [We Do | Guided practice | Grammar | HITS 7]

you_do.title: Add the given adverbial
you_do.rule: Rewrite each sentence with the detail given. Comma only when the detail is at the front.
you_do.example: One done for you: We waited. + after lunch -> After lunch, we waited.
items: A) The lights flickered. + before the storm
B) Mia checked her answers. + with real care
you_do.footer: Front takes a comma. End takes none.
you_do.notes:
ANSWER: A - Before the storm, the lights flickered. B - Mia checked her answers with real care.
1. SAY: "Use the worked example. Put A's detail at the front and B's detail at the end."
2. TIME: 90 seconds. Work on your own board.
3. CIRCULATE: if a student is stuck, SAY: "Look where after lunch moved in the example. Now find the when detail in A." Then start A together.
4. SCAN every board. 80%+ -> reveal the check slide. Less -> finish A together, rub it out, then re-ask A.
TRAP: forgetting A's comma or adding one in B. Fix: name the position first, then repair the punctuation.
STRETCH: Move B's detail to the front and explain what changes.
HELP: Give both sentence openings; students finish them from the printed words.
---
Purpose: fixed-answer practice adding a detail in both positions. [You Do | Independent practice | Grammar | HITS 5]
you_do.check_title: Tick it or fix it - Add the given adverbial
you_do.check_rule: Tick each complete sentence. Fix the position or the comma if it differs.
check_items: A) Before the storm, the lights flickered.
Fronted when detail, so it takes a comma.
B) Mia checked her answers with real care.
End how detail, so no comma is needed.
you_do.check_footer: Name the job and the position before the comma
you_do.check_notes:
ANSWER: A - Before the storm, the lights flickered. B - Mia checked her answers with real care.
1. REVEAL after all boards are scanned. MODEL: SAY: "Before the storm tells when and sits at the front, so I place a comma after it."
2. SAY: "Tick each complete sentence. Fix any position or comma that differs."
3. ASK: "Why does B need no comma?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: the detail is at the end.
4. SCAN corrections. 80%+ -> continue. Less -> compare each answer with the worked example, then re-check.
TRAP: ticking correct words with the wrong punctuation. Fix: point to the position, then repair the comma.
HELP: read the green reason line before checking the punctuation.
---
Purpose: model the position-and-comma reasoning before feedback. [You Do | Feedback | Grammar]

sessions.wtr_new_notes:
READ each word as it appears. -ULE makes the thing SMALL.
nodule - nod means knot + -ULE means small: a small knot or lump, like the ones on a plant root.
capsule - caps means box + -ULE means small: a small box that holds something safely inside.
granule - gran means grain + -ULE means small: one small grain, like a grain of sugar or sand.
molecule - mol means mass + -ULE means small: a very small piece of mass, the smallest part of a substance.
module - mod means measure + -ULE means small: a small measured part built to join onto others.
minuscule - minus means less + -ULE means small: less than small, so it is barely there at all.
globule - glob means ball + -ULE means small: a small ball or drop of liquid.
ovule - ov means egg + -ULE means small: the small egg inside a plant that can grow into a seed.
tubule - tub means tube + -ULE means small: a very small tube, like the ones inside your kidneys.
Memory hook: three jobs this week - -ACY names a state, -ULE makes it small, MEGA- makes it a million. Today, hear -ULE and shrink it.
SOURCES: -ule card meaning and word family from the photographed Yoshimoto suffix card; globule and ovule are logged verified additions.

grammar.header_notes:
PURPOSE: Add an adverbial that tells how or why, building on yesterday's when detail.
PREP: Whiteboards out before the I do.

i_do.title: Add a how or why detail
i_do.rule: An adverbial tells when, where, how or why. A fronted adverbial takes a comma.
i_do.example: We sealed the capsule. + to protect the sample -> We sealed the capsule to protect the sample.
items: To protect the sample tells WHY.
It sits at the end, so it needs no comma.
i_do.routine: Eyes on me - listen for the reason
i_do.footer: Ask why, then add the reason
i_do.notes:
ANSWER: We sealed the capsule to protect the sample.
1. SAY: "An adverbial tells when, where, how or why. Yesterday we added a when detail; today we add a why detail."
2. MODEL: Point to to protect the sample. SAY: "I ask myself why we sealed it, and that group of words answers me."
3. ASK: "What does to protect the sample tell us?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: why.
4. ASK: "Why is there no comma this time?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: the detail is at the end.
TRAP: hearing why but writing a when detail. Fix: ask the why question aloud, then reread the words you chose.
---
Purpose: restate the rule, then model a why detail at the end. [I Do | Explicit modelling | Grammar | HITS 3]

we_do.title: Add the reason
we_do.rule: Add the given why detail, then check the punctuation.
we_do.example: The class left the room. + because the alarm sounded
items: Write the whole new sentence.
Decide whether a comma is needed.
we_do.footer: Stem: It tells why because it gives the reason
we_do.notes:
ANSWER: The class left the room because the alarm sounded. No comma is needed.
1. SAY: "Thumbs up when you know where the detail goes. Then write it... chin it... show me."
2. TIME: 20 seconds, then every board up together.
3. SCAN the middle rows first. 80%+ -> take the reason. Less -> say the sentence aloud together, then re-collect all boards.
4. ASK: "How do you know those words tell why?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: they give the reason the class left.

sessions.wtr_new_notes:
READ each word as it appears. MEGA- means a MILLION, every single time.
megahertz - MEGA- means million + hertz means cycles each second: a million cycles every second.
megawatt - MEGA- means million + watt means a unit of power: a million watts of power.
megaton - MEGA- means million + ton means a unit of weight: the force of a million tonnes of explosive.
megaunit - MEGA- means million + unit means one measured amount: a million of those units counted together.
megabyte - MEGA- means million + byte means a small block of computer data: a million bytes of data.
megalitre - MEGA- means million + litre means a unit of liquid: a million litres, the way our reservoirs are measured.
megajoule - MEGA- means million + joule means a unit of energy: a million joules of energy.
megapixel - MEGA- means million + pixel means one dot in a picture: a million tiny dots in one photo.
megavolt - MEGA- means million + volt means a unit of electrical push: a million volts pushing a current along.
Memory hook: three jobs this week - -ACY names a state, -ULE makes it small, MEGA- makes it a million. Today, hear MEGA- and think one million.
SOURCES: mega- card meaning from the photographed Yoshimoto prefix card; four SI additions are logged verified exceptions.
